scripts.radio:
Hamjambo and welcome to Kenya on Record. Let us examine the decisions and numbers shaping public accountability this week.

First, at the Milimani Law Courts, a clerk attached to the Kenya Revenue Authority was arraigned over an alleged eight point five million shilling fraud. The prosecution points to revenue diversion through manipulated tax records. It is a sobering development. While ordinary citizens tighten their belts to comply with every statutory deduction, systemic leaks within our revenue collection agency severely undermine public confidence. True reform at KRA cannot just be about setting higher targets; it must mean water-tight internal systems that hold every officer accountable.

Meanwhile, critical conversations around future elections are taking shape. Rigathi Gachagua and the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission have set talks for this Thursday to deliberate on election technology and the issuance of national identity cards. With voter registration fundamentally tied to obtaining an ID, civil society and citizens are watching closely. The core demand remains straightforward: election technology must be transparent and verifiable, and no eligible youth should be disenfranchised by bureaucratic delays at registration bureaus.

Kwa ufupi: Karani mmoja wa KRA amefikishwa mahakamani kwa madai ya kufuja shilingi milioni nane nukta tano za ushuru. Wakati huo huo, Rigathi Gachagua na IEBC wanatazamiwa kukutana Alhamisi hii kujadili masuala ya teknolojia ya uchaguzi na utoaji wa vitambulisho vya kitaifa.

Stay engaged, verify the facts, and keep duty bearers on record.
scripts.voice_note: Habari yenu, this is Kenya on Record with your weekly brief. Two key accountability stories are on our radar. First, a KRA clerk has been charged in court over an alleged fraud of 8.5 million shillings through altered tax systems. When ordinary Kenyans are paying every single coin demanded by law, internal revenue leaks cannot be treated as business as usual. Second, on our electoral integrity: Rigathi Gachagua and the IEBC are meeting this Thursday to discuss election technology and national ID issuance. Your national ID is your right and your voter registration pass. Technology must safeguard the ballot, not invite suspicion. Let us watch what commitments come out of that meeting. Share this note and stay alert.
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe: Always pay KRA taxes via official government paybills only. Never hand cash or send money to an individual clerk's personal number. Verify receipts.
scripts.reels: Eight point five million shillings. That is the sum a KRA clerk is accused of siphoning through manipulated tax records. While millions of hardworking Kenyans pay their dues down to the very last shilling, public trust erodes when internal controls fail. We are tracking this case at Milimani to see where systemic accountability begins. Follow Kenya on Record.
